title: A benchmark proves routing by verdict pays
goal: `benchmarks.py run route-by-verdict` runs kb_ask.py's routing (agent_bench.route, following kb_ask.plan's web and split routes) against the bare Sonnet web arm and the kb Sonnet arm on s5_none, o1_offkb, s8_falsegood2, h2_applock, s1_fact and s3_multi, with full model names, and benchmarks.csv holds its record; its report section gives per case (the route each question's pack takes on the run's commit: web, split, good) each arm's mean cost and time, the spend, and says for each case whether the operator's bar holds: web within 10% of the bare arm's cost, split below both other arms, good on the reader route as before.
notes: Operator budget: paid runs up to $10 for this story. Within 10% of bare on none is the bar the operator set; a miss is a finding for the review (a bug), not a reason to change the bar. The case of each question is the route its pack takes on the run's commit, not a fixed label: s8_falsegood2 packs `none` on HEAD now, not a flagged good. The kb Sonnet arm follows the server instructions, hence the dependency on ST-uuaooyrm; the kb: hook and the query log are not measured here. `--model` aliases move, so a reproducible benchmark pins the full name (claude/ci-and-headless.md:85, DOC S-ezqg74ki). The last two checks pass now: they guard the report and the benchmark tests.
